criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs builds a reader brief with job planning disabled and asserts the brief names reader, producer and verifier as enabled roles and does not list planner or critic as enabled; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
criteria.evidence: New test `the_reader_brief_lists_only_reader_producer_and_verifier_when_job_planning_is_off` renders the brief with enabled_roles = [reader, producer, verifier]. It takes the text under ENABLED_ROLES_HEADING, asserts it contains "reader, producer, verifier." and asserts it contains neither "planner" nor "critic". It passed when I ran it, and so did the other 8 reader-brief tests.

criteria.criterion: A second test builds the brief with job planning enabled and asserts planner and critic appear in the enabled-roles section; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
criteria.evidence: New test `the_reader_brief_lists_planner_and_critic_when_job_planning_is_on` sets all five roles and asserts the section contains "reader, planner, critic, producer, verifier.". It passed when I ran it.

criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core (e.g. reading.rs tests) shows read_once/reader input construction derives the role list from the config's [job_plan] enabled value, not a hard-coded list; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: `the_reader_input_roles_come_from_the_config_job_plan_enabled_value` loads the shipped athena.toml and toggles job_plan.enabled between true, false and None. It asserts that `Config::enabled_roles` includes planner and critic only when enabled is true. It also checks the source text for `enabled_roles: jc.config.enabled_roles(),` in read_once. It passed, as did the athena-data test `enabled_roles_follow_the_job_plan_enabled_value`. The read_once part is a source-text check, not a rendered brief from the real pipeline (see findings).

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs READING_RULES contains a new rule stating that brief content targets only enabled roles, marked `(prose only)`, and the array length and existing length assertions are updated consistently.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. READING_RULES is now `[&str; 10]` with the new line "Enabled roles: brief content targets only the roles listed under Enabled roles; a role not listed gets no new content (prose only)." The length assertion was changed from 9 to 10, a new assertion requires a prose-only Enabled roles line, and the section-size limit went from 2750 to 2900 bytes with the comment updated.

criteria.criterion: No unrelated behavior changes: `cargo test` passes with all existing tests, `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
criteria.evidence: Athena's records for 2db4f70c92d2 show fmt, clippy and the tests passed in CI run 42500466031. The diff changes no behavior beyond the new field, the new section and the new rule line; it is purely additive.

findings.summary: The athena-core test checks read_once's wiring by searching the source text rather than by inspecting a brief produced by the pipeline.
findings.evidence: The test asserts `reading_source().contains("enabled_roles: jc.config.enabled_roles(),")`. run_pin_tests.rs already captures real reader briefs (for example `briefs[0]` near line 1997), so an end-to-end test could set [job_plan] enabled and check the brief's Enabled roles section, as the behavior-evidence default prefers. Config::enabled_roles itself is covered by real tests, so the risk is low.

findings.summary: One expected deliverable was not modified.
findings.evidence: The deliverables list says modify, but the diff does not touch this file. It was not needed: the only ReaderInputs builders are in reading.rs and the briefs.rs tests, and CI passed. No file outside the list was changed.

summary: The change does what was asked, and I recommend accepting it. The reader's brief now has an "# Enabled roles" section, filled in by read_once from the effective config through a new `Config::enabled_roles`. Reader, producer and verifier are always listed; planner and critic are listed only when `[job_plan] enabled` is true. READING_RULES gains a tenth rule, marked prose only, saying brief content targets only the enabled roles, and the length assertion was updated to match. I ran the new tests: the two brief tests in athena-context (planning off, planning on), the athena-core test and the athena-data config test all pass. CI passed fmt, clippy and the full test suite. CHANGELOG.md names the root cause: the reader was never told which roles run. The change stays inside the expected deliverables and touches no prompts, refusal checks or config files. The one weakness is minor: the athena-core test confirms read_once's wiring by searching the source text, not by checking a brief produced by the real pipeline, though the existing pipeline tests could do that.
